Lidar is a technology for obtaining and data processing about distant objects using active optical systems that use the phenomena of absorption and scattering of light in optically transparent media. Lidar advantage over other optical scanners is the ability to work in the absence of illumination since the lidar is itself a source of invisible light. The most commonly used method is simultaneous localization and map building (SLAM - Simultaneous Localization and Mapping). The above method used in mobile autonomous means for building a map in an unknown space or for updating a map in a previously known space with simultaneous control of the current location and distance traveled [27, 28]. Popular methods for approximate solving this problem include a particle filter and an advanced Kalman filter. Obstacle detection is one of the main sub-tasks of the SLAM method. In this report, the authors propose a fast and accurate algorithm for the structural separation of obstacles in the field, focused on traffic conditions in agricultural fieldwork.
